text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Daggers were drawn out at Zimbabwe's trade promotion body Zimtrade this week as a power struggle emerged pitting chief executive Morrison Sifelani against Zimtrade's directors and Industry and Commerce minister Nathan Shamuyarira.
- North Korean diplomat Jang Myong Sik, arrested by Zimbabwe last month over charges of illegally possessing ivory, is apparently hiding at his country's embassy in Harare.

- An emerging Zimbabwean conglomerate, Randalls Holdings, will seek a listing on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange in March in a development expected to help satisfy the current huge investor appetite for equities.

- Pyramid money clubs will be banned in Zimbabwe, with fines of up to Z$1 million and jail terms of up to 10 years imposed on those that operate them, once a bill to be tabled before parliament in March becomes law.
- The Zimbabwe International Travel Expo 1997 opens in the capital Harare on Thursday and will be attended by a record 120 foreign buyers.

- South African President Nelson Mandela arrives in Harare on Thursday morning for talks with his Zimbabwean counterpart Robert Mugabe, during which they are expected to discuss regional and international issues.
